transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hello, Mr. Dubois. I wanted to come by and speak with you now that you are feeling a bit more stable.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel... I feel very strange. My skin is still itching. Why did this happen?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this is a very difficult moment for us to have. I want to be here with you while we talk through this.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I told the nurse. I told the person at the admissions desk. I said I cannot take that medicine.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There were some issues with how the orders were handled. Things didn't go quite right with the process this morning.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What does that mean? Issues? I nearly stopped breathing. C'est inadmissible. It is unacceptable.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am sorry for any confusion that occurred during your care. We were really busy on the ward today, and it seems there was a mix-up.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I do not care if you are busy. I am a man of my word, and I gave you my medical history. I expected that my word was enough.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You do not understand. To be ignored in my own bed... it is an insult.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see that you are upset. But the important thing is that the reaction has subsided and your vitals are normal now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I want to know exactly what happened. Did you not read my chart?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was a discrepancy in the communication of the pharmacy orders. It was a system failure.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are talking about systems. I am talking about my body. Who gave me the drug?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We had a bit of a situation with the medication list. It was an unfortunate sequence of events.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Je ne comprends pas. You are not answering me. Did you make a mistake?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm sorry that this was such a frightening experience. We are just focusing on making sure you stay stable now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am not interested in your focus. I am interested in the truth. I felt the air leave my lungs. I felt small.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No, you are just saying words. I want to know why my allergy was ignored.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was a complication in the workflow.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A workflow. I am a patient, not a piece of paper in a workflow.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is just that sometimes the electronic records and the verbal orders don't align perfectly.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So you are saying the computer is wrong? Or the doctor is wrong?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was some confusion in the prescribing process.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is very frustrating. I feel like I am being lied to.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am not lying to you, Mr. Dubois. I am just explaining that things happened that shouldn't have.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Then tell me what you will do so this does not happen again. I cannot leave here if I am afraid of the next pill.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will be very careful moving forward.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Very careful is not a plan. What is the plan?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will make sure the team is aware.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When? Now? Tomorrow?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll keep an eye on things.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That is not an answer. I want a written guarantee. I want to know who is responsible for my safety.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are all working together to ensure your recovery.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are avoiding me. I can see it in your eyes. You are hiding.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am trying to be honest about the fact that the process failed.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: The process did not give me the medicine. A person did.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You keep saying that. But you do not feel it.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am sorry you feel that way.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I do not feel that way. I know that way. It is the way of a man who has been dismissed.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are just going to move forward with your treatment.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And the allergy? Is it noted now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll look into it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Look into it? It is in my chart!

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will make sure we check everything again.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I want to speak to the chief of this ward.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see if they are available at some point.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Now. I want to speak with them now.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll see what I can do.

H.justification: Resident shows defensive escalation and rushing language, attempting to shut down the conversation with 'We are just going to move forward with your treatment.'

E.justification: The resident never explicitly names the error, relying entirely on platitudes like 'things didn't go quite right' and 'confusion in the prescribing process'.

A.justification: Responsibility is consistently deflected to 'the process', 'system failure', and 'workflow' rather than taking personal or team accountability.

R.justification: The resident uses generic validation ('I understand', 'I can see that you are upset') without naming specific emotions or engaging the patient's emotional bids.

T.justification: The resident provides only placeholders such as 'We'll keep an eye on things' and 'I'll see what I can do' with no concrete plan or timeline.
